questions.stem: Consider the following statements about the OFFICE OF PRESIDENT of India. 1. The President is elected by an Electoral College consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament AND elected members of State Legislative Assemblies (including the NCT of Delhi and the UT of Puducherry). 2. The value of the vote of an MLA depends on the population of the state (as per the 1971 Census, by the 84th Amendment). 3. A person cannot be elected President unless they are qualified to be elected to the Lok Sabha. 4. The President can be removed only by impeachment for 'violation of the Constitution' under Article 61. Which are correct?

options.option_text: 1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 4 only
2 and 3 only

questions.explanation: All four correct. Electoral College: elected MPs of both Houses + elected MLAs (nominated members are EXCLUDED). 1971 Census frozen value by 84th Amendment (2001). Qualifications mirror LS member qualifications + 35 age. Article 61 lays down the impeachment procedure, requiring a ¼-member notice, 14-day notice, and a 2/3-of-the-total-membership majority in each House.

questions.stem: ASSERTION (A): The Governor of a state can withhold assent to a bill passed by the state legislature and reserve it for the consideration of the President. REASON (R): Under Article 200, the Governor has four options — assent, withhold assent, return for reconsideration, or reserve for the President.

options.option_text: Both A and R are true, R is the correct explanation
Both A and R are true, R is NOT the correct explanation
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true

questions.explanation: Article 200 lists exactly the four options in R, and A specifically describes the 'withhold / reserve for President' option. The Supreme Court (2024 judgement in State of Punjab v. Governor) held that 'as soon as possible' in Art. 200 must be interpreted as a reasonable time frame — Governors cannot sit on bills indefinitely.

questions.stem: Which of the following provisions was NOT introduced by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992) establishing Panchayati Raj?

options.option_text: Reservation of seats for SCs and STs in proportion to their population
Minimum 33% reservation for women
Five-year tenure for panchayats and holding elections within 6 months of dissolution
Creation of Urban Local Bodies (Municipalities) in every state

questions.explanation: Urban Local Bodies (Municipalities) were created by the 74th Amendment (1992), not the 73rd. The 73rd dealt only with RURAL local government (Panchayati Raj), while the 74th dealt with URBAN local government (Nagar Panchayats / Municipal Councils / Municipal Corporations). All other provisions listed are correctly credited to the 73rd.

questions.stem: Consider the following about the ELECTION COMMISSION OF INDIA (ECI). 1. It is a constitutional body established under Article 324. 2. The Chief Election Commissioner and other Commissioners are appointed by the President. 3. The CEC can only be removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge. 4. Other Election Commissioners can be removed only on the recommendation of the CEC. Which are correct?

options.option_text: 1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 4 only

questions.explanation: All four are correct. ECI is constitutional (Art. 324). CEC + ECs appointed by President (post the 2023 Act, from a panel recommended by a committee of PM, LoP, CJI/nominee). CEC's removal parity with SC judge (impeachment). Other ECs can be removed only by President on CEC's recommendation — a built-in check. 2023 Act (replacing the earlier SC-recommended committee structure under Anoop Baranwal 2023) is current law; SC matter still under challenge.

questions.stem: A state government passes a law on a subject in the CONCURRENT LIST that conflicts with an existing Central law on the same subject. The state law was passed AFTER receiving the President's assent. Which of the following is TRUE?

options.option_text: The state law is void because Central law always prevails on Concurrent List subjects.
The state law prevails in that state, except to the extent Parliament subsequently amends or repeals it (Article 254(2) exception).
The state law needs ratification by Rajya Sabha to be valid.
The state law is void because concurrent subjects can only be legislated on by Parliament.

questions.explanation: Under Article 254(1), if a state law on a Concurrent subject conflicts with Central law, the Central law prevails. BUT Article 254(2) creates an exception — if the state law has been reserved for and received the PRESIDENT's ASSENT, it prevails in that state. Parliament can however still over-ride later by amendment/repeal.

questions.stem: Match the constitutional body with its founding Article.

options.option_text: ECI-324, CAG-148, UPSC-315, Finance Commission-280
ECI-148, CAG-324, UPSC-280, Finance Commission-315
ECI-324, CAG-280, UPSC-148, Finance Commission-315
ECI-315, CAG-324, UPSC-148, Finance Commission-280

questions.explanation: ECI — Article 324. CAG — Article 148. UPSC — Article 315 (also governs State PSCs). Finance Commission — Article 280 (constituted every 5 years). These four Article-body pairs are among the highest-frequency exam recall items.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a 'money bill' under Article 110?

options.option_text: Imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of any tax.
Declaration of any expenditure as 'charged on the Consolidated Fund'.
A bill for the appropriation of money out of the Contingency Fund.
A bill regulating the borrowing of money by the Government of India.

questions.explanation: Article 110 enumerates the CONSOLIDATED FUND, not the Contingency Fund, for money-bill purposes. Appropriation from the Contingency Fund is regulated by Article 267 but doesn't make a bill a 'money bill' under Art. 110. The Speaker's certification under Art. 110(3) is 'final'.

options.option_text: A law that discriminates on the basis of colour or race.
A legislation which, though appearing to be within the competence of a legislature, in substance encroaches on a field reserved for another legislature.
A special Presidential decree during Emergency.
A law passed by a state subject to central approval.

questions.explanation: 'What cannot be done directly cannot be done indirectly.' Classic phrasing in K.C. Gajapati Narayan Deo vs State of Orissa (1953). The legislature cannot dress up a law that is actually outside its competence as one within its competence by clever drafting. Used to strike down state laws that trespass on Union List fields, or vice versa.
